The mouse, the controller and the keys.

How far the view turns as the mouse moves, on Counter-Strike 2's scale: your CS2 number turns the same here. Drag the slider, or press left and right. Click the number (or press A) to type an exact value, e.g. 1.7, then press Enter.|No acceleration.
How far the view turns up and down, of how far it turns side to side. 1X turns it as far.
How fast you turn while zoomed in. CS2 matches Counter-Strike 2's scoped feel; Original is how Halo felt.|Mouse only: controllers always turn as Halo did.
Moving the mouse forward looks down, as a flight stick does.
Slows and drags your aim along with a target while you aim with the mouse, as it does with a controller.|Off in Pro 2v2 games, for everyone.
Turns the view the moment the mouse moves, not up to two of the game's updates later. Off feels as the original did.|Off for everyone in a Pro 2v2 Classic game; yours again after it.
The menus' blue arrow for the mouse, and its size. The sizes keep their share of the screen at any resolution.|Off shows the system's pointer.
The keys and mouse buttons for each action, two for each.
The buttons the HUD's prompts show. Auto shows the keys or the controller's buttons, as you last played with.
The look sensitivity and inversion, the button and stick layouts, and vibration, kept in your player profile.
Your hands, aiming, turning, your height, the HUD and the menus in VR.
Hold crouches while the button is held, as Halo did. Toggle crouches at a tap until you press it again, jump, take a seat or die; holding it still crouches while held.
Off: a full push of the stick stands you up from a crouch, as Halo did. On: you stay crouched and walk at a crouch's speed.|The touch controls always stay crouched.
The touch controls' Crouch. Toggle crouches at a tap until the next tap, a jump, a seat or death; Hold crouches while your finger is on it.
